tracks.narration: Flip a switch onto an inductor — and the current refuses to jump. What's stopping it?
Battery V in series with a resistor R and an inductor L. Close the switch — current starts to rise, but the inductor pushes back.
The current rises along an exponential curve toward V over R, while the voltage across the inductor decays from V down to zero — perfect mirror images.
Tau equals L over R is the time constant. After one tau the current has reached sixty three percent of its final value. After five tau it is essentially full.
Bigger L slows the rise; bigger R hurries it. The time constant L over R sets the rhythm — the exact opposite trade-off from R C.
